content:
maria: :warning: Heads up — since 08:13UTC we're seeing a wave of 429s from eu-west-1. Autoscaler briefly flapped and fleet saturation propagated back to callers. SDK clients are retrying aggressively and amplifying load.

maria: Sample response we saw in logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 08:13:35 GMT
X-Queue-Length: 120
X-Available-GPUs: 0
X-Request-ID: rwd-req-8a7f
```

maria: Problem: SDKs expect numeric Retry-After seconds and treat HTTP-date as parse error -> immediate retry. Also no consistent header indicating "shed" vs "throttle" so clients guess and hammer. @sre-oncall can you confirm? :eyes:

kevin: Confirmed. We had an older nginx layer that emitted HTTP-date. New plan was seconds but it didn't roll to all frontends.

lina: SDK note: current JS/Go SDKs parse Retry-After leniently but fall back to immediate retry if parse fails. That behavior is dangerous.

alex: Proposal: standardize on seconds-form Retry-After (e.g. "Retry-After: 3") and add 2 explicit headers:
- `X-Redwood-Backpressure: none|throttle|shed|drain`
- `X-Redwood-Queue-Estimate: <integer>` (approx queued requests)
Also include `X-Pool-Id` so SDKs can decide whether to back off or try a different pool/region.

jules: +1. If we expose `shed` vs `throttle`, SDK can treat `shed` as non-retriable (fail fast) and `throttle` as retryable with backoff.

sdk-team: Actionable SDK changes:
- treat Retry-After HTTP-date as valid but prefer seconds; if unparsable, DO NOT retry immediately (fail once, surface to app).
- if `X-Redwood-Backpressure: shed` -> return error to caller without retry.
- if `throttle` -> apply exponential backoff with full jitter scaled to Retry-After when present.
- cap retries and expose telemetry to customer.

sre-oncall: We'll roll a patch to frontends to always emit seconds form on Retry-After and add the two headers. Targeting a staged rollout in eu-west-1 in the next 30m. Will also add `X-Redwood-Nodepool: <id>` (friendly short id) for debugging.

kevin: One caution: clients doing region-fallback cause cross-region egress and $$$. Recommend SDK default: randomize retry window + prefer same-region if header `X-Redwood-Backpressure` present instead of immediate region failover.

lina: Agreed. SDK change: if backpressure seen and pool id present, do not trigger region failover for the first N retries; instead do jittered backoff and respect Retry-After.

maria: From infra side: this also affects autoscaler thresholds. If SDKs back off properly we can avoid aggressive scale-ups that increase cost. We should include a telemetry tag `x-client-backoff-applied: true` in the next SDK release so infra can correlate.

jules: Small extras: include `X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset` epoch seconds for optional use (helps long windows). Also consider a boolean `X-Redwood-DoNotRetry` for immediate client-side failfast situations.

sdk-team: We'll implement: respect `Retry-After` seconds, honor `X-Redwood-Backpressure` semantics, no region failover for first 3 retries, and surface a metric `sdk.backoff_applied{region,pool}`. PR incoming in ~2 days.

deploy-bot: deploys/frontend-retry-headers v1.2 started (canary eu-west-1)

maria: Action items summary:
- infra (@sre-oncall): emit seconds Retry-After + X-Redwood-Backpressure + X-Redwood-Queue-Estimate + X-Redwood-Nodepool (canary now)
- SDK (@sdk-team): change backoff logic to respect headers, avoid immediate region-fallback, add telemetry tag
- platform (@maria, @kevin): update docs and runbook for handling SDK 429 patterns and cost implications

kevin: I'll draft a short runbook blurb for oncall: what to look for (high queue-estimate, many 429->retries, cross-region storms) and quick mitigations (scale target adjustment, fail-open for non-critical workloads).

maria: Thanks all. Will monitor canary and post an update in 15m. :thumbsup:
